usageNotes: Use this to permanently remove a specific TFA entry (TOTP, WebAuthn, recovery key, etc.) from a user account. Either an admin with Access.Modify privilege or the user themselves can call this — the optional password parameter is required by the server when the caller is self-managing and root@pam is not the requestor (server-side enforcement varies by realm). Obtain the entry id first via the corresponding GET /access/tfa/{userid} list call.

examples.summary: Remove a TOTP entry from a domain user's account

destructiveReason: Permanently deletes the TFA entry; the user will lose access to that second factor immediately and cannot recover it.
tips: Retrieve the full list of a user's TFA entries with GET /access/tfa/{userid} before deleting to confirm the correct id.
If the user has only one TFA entry and the realm enforces MFA, removing it may lock the user out — verify realm policy first.
API tokens (allowtoken: true) are permitted to make this call, so automation scripts can remove stale keys during offboarding.
